## Hypothesis

Autorearch sweeps can waste significant compute when the underlying signal's win rate is far below the gate's minimum acceptable threshold. A pre-flight sanity check that estimates baseline win rate from a cheap pilot run and aborts the sweep if the gap to the gate floor exceeds 20% prevents wasted GPU/CPU cycles and focuses research on promising regions of parameter space.

## Mechanism

Before launching a full parameter sweep, run a limited pilot (e.g., 10 random parameter combos) using the same backtest engine as the sweep. Compute the pilot's win rate (WR). If `gate_floor - pilot_WR > 0.20 * gate_floor` (i.e., gap >20% of gate floor), abort the sweep and log the decision. Otherwise, proceed with the full sweep. The gate floor is taken from the sweep's configuration (e.g., min_win_rate = 0.55). The pilot uses the same data slice (in-sample) as the sweep to ensure comparability.
